entries.description_source_en: These Pokémon nest in the ground and use their tusks to crush hard berries. Crushing berries is also how they test each other’s strength.
entries.fact_source_en: They play with each other by knocking their large tusks together. Their tusks break sometimes, but they grow back so quickly that it isn’t a concern.

entries.description_source_en: After battle, this Pokémon carefully sharpens its tusks on river rocks. It needs to take care of its tusks—if one breaks, it will never grow back.
entries.fact_source_en: Its skin is as hard as a suit of armor. Fraxure’s favorite strategy is to tackle its opponents, stabbing them with its tusks at the same time.

entries.description_source_en: Its resilient tusks are its pride and joy. It licks up dirt to take in the minerals it needs to keep its tusks in top condition.
entries.fact_source_en: While usually kindhearted, it can be terrifying if angered. Tusks that can slice through steel beams are how Haxorus deals with its adversaries.

entries.description_source_en: When this Pokémon is in good health, its snot becomes thicker and stickier. It will smear its snot on anyone it doesn’t like.
entries.fact_source_en: Their snot is a barometer of health. When healthy, their snot is sticky and the power of their ice moves increases.

entries.description_source_en: It swims through frigid seas, searching for prey. From its frozen breath, it forms icy fangs that are harder than steel.
entries.fact_source_en: It swims energetically through frigid seas. When it gets tired, it freezes the seawater with its breath so it can rest on the ice.

entries.description_source_en: With its icy chains, Cryogonal freezes those it encounters. It then takes its victims away to somewhere unknown.
entries.fact_source_en: They are composed of ice crystals. They capture prey with chains of ice, freezing the prey at -148 degrees Fahrenheit.

entries.description_source_en: When attacked, it tightly shuts the lid of its shell. This reaction fails to protect it from Karrablast, however, because they can still get into the shell.
entries.fact_source_en: It has a strange physiology that responds to electricity. When together with Karrablast, Shelmet evolves for some reason.

entries.description_source_en: It moves with blinding speed and lobs poison at foes. Featuring Accelgor as a main character is a surefire way to make a movie or comic popular.
entries.fact_source_en: When its body dries out, it weakens. So, to prevent dehydration, it wraps itself in many layers of thin membrane.

entries.description_source_en: Thanks to bacteria that lived in the mud flats with it, this Pokémon developed the organs it uses to generate electricity.
entries.fact_source_en: For some reason, this Pokémon smiles slightly when it emits a strong electric current from the yellow markings on its body.

entries.description_source_en: In one minute, a well-trained Mienfoo can chop with its arms more than 100 times.
entries.fact_source_en: Though small, Mienfoo’s temperament is fierce. Any creature that approaches Mienfoo carelessly will be greeted with a flurry of graceful attacks.

entries.description_source_en: When Mienshao comes across a truly challenging opponent, it will lighten itself by biting off the fur on its arms.
entries.fact_source_en: When Mienshao lets out a bizarre wail, you’re in danger. A flurry of kicks and chops too fast to see is about to be unleashed!

entries.description_source_en: Druddigon lives in caves, but it never skips sunbathing—it won’t be able to move if its body gets too cold.
entries.fact_source_en: Druddigon are vicious and cunning. They take up residence in nests dug out by other Pokémon, treating the stolen nests as their own lairs.

entries.description_source_en: They were sculpted from clay in ancient times. No one knows why, but some of them are driven to continually line up boulders.
entries.fact_source_en: This Pokémon was created from clay. It received orders from its master many thousands of years ago, and it still follows those orders to this day.

entries.description_source_en: Artillery platforms built into the walls of ancient castles served as perches from which Golurk could fire energy beams.
entries.fact_source_en: There’s a theory that inside Golurk is a perpetual motion machine that produces limitless energy, but this belief hasn’t been proven.

entries.description_source_en: It uses river stones to maintain the cutting edges of the blades covering its body. These sharpened blades allow it to bring down opponents.
entries.fact_source_en: It follows Bisharp’s orders to a tee when it attacks enemies. After slashing an opponent, Pawniard clangs both of its blades together.

entries.description_source_en: It’s accompanied by a large retinue of Pawniard. Bisharp keeps a keen eye on its minions, ensuring none of them even think of double-crossing it.
entries.fact_source_en: No matter how strong the Bisharp, it’s said that if the blade on its head is chipped, it will retire from its position as the boss.

entries.description_source_en: These Pokémon can crush a car with no more than a headbutt. Bouffalant with more hair on their heads hold higher positions within the herd.
entries.fact_source_en: These Pokémon live in herds of about 20 individuals. Bouffalant that betray the herd will lose the hair on their heads for some reason.

entries.description_source_en: Its chick-like looks belie its hotheadedness. It challenges its parents at every opportunity, desperate to prove its strength.
entries.fact_source_en: With its sharp claws, this Pokémon pierces its prey, and then it pecks at them. Although it also consumes berries, it’s a carnivore at heart.

entries.description_source_en: Screaming a bloodcurdling battle cry, this huge and ferocious bird Pokémon goes out on the hunt. It blasts lakes with shock waves, then scoops up any prey that float to the water's surface.
entries.fact_source_en: With its brave disposition, it fears nothing—not even death. Ancient Alolan people respected it, referring to it as “the hero of the sky.”

entries.description_source_en: It wears a bone to protect its rear. It often squabbles with others of its kind over particularly comfy bones.
entries.fact_source_en: Mandibuzz gives it the bones it wears. Vullaby’s wings are short, so it can’t fly yet, but it jumps around, dreaming of wide open skies.

entries.description_source_en: Although it’s a bit of a ruffian, this Pokémon will take lost Vullaby under its wing and care for them till they’re ready to leave the nest.
entries.fact_source_en: They adorn themselves beautifully with bones. This is supposedly an effort to attract males, but no male Mandibuzz have ever been found.

entries.description_source_en: There’s a hole in its tail that allows it to draw in the air it needs to keep its fire burning. If the hole gets blocked, this Pokémon will fall ill.
entries.fact_source_en: It draws in air through its tail, transforms it into fire, and uses it like a tongue. It melts Durant and eats them.

entries.description_source_en: They lay their eggs deep inside their nests. When attacked by Heatmor, they retaliate using their massive mandibles.
entries.fact_source_en: With their large mandibles, these Pokémon can crunch their way through rock. They work together to protect their eggs from Sandaconda.

entries.description_source_en: When it encounters something, its first urge is usually to bite it. If it likes what it tastes, it will commit the associated scent to memory.
entries.fact_source_en: Because it can’t see, this Pokémon is constantly biting at everything it touches, trying to keep track of its surroundings.

entries.description_source_en: While hunting for prey, Zweilous wanders its territory, its two heads often bickering over which way to go.
entries.fact_source_en: Their two heads will fight each other over a single piece of food. Zweilous are covered in scars even without battling others.
